subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can quantities with magnitude and direction be represented and combined through vector operations in three-dimensional space?
in_scope_units: 10.2 Some Basic Concepts: directed segments, magnitude, position vectors and direction cosines.
10.4 Addition of Vectors: triangle and parallelogram laws.
10.5 Multiplication of a Vector by a Scalar and components of a vector.
Section formula and vector joining two points.
10.6 Product of Two Vectors: scalar product, projections and vector product.
banned_topics: Matrices and determinants as separate chapters

known_pitfalls.claim: Any quantity with a numerical value is a vector.
known_pitfalls.correction: A vector must have both magnitude and direction; a scalar has magnitude only.

known_pitfalls.claim: Equal vectors must have the same initial point.
known_pitfalls.correction: Equal vectors need only have the same magnitude and direction because the chapter treats free vectors.

known_pitfalls.claim: The dot product is a vector.
known_pitfalls.correction: The scalar product is a scalar.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Example 2 to classify scalar and vector quantities.
Use NCERT Example 6 to find a unit vector from components.
Use the section-formula example to divide a line segment internally.
Use a scalar-product example to find an angle or projection.
Use a vector-product example to find area or a perpendicular vector.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 10.1 to 10.4 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 10.
